en/1-getting-started/01-why-this-plugin.title: 1.1 – Why this plugin
en/1-getting-started/01-why-this-plugin.content:
What Quartz ships
The explorer shows the content folder as a tree in the sidebar, with collapsible folders it
remembers. For a digital garden that is exactly right: you see everything, and you find everything.
For a website with sections it is not enough. It knows one form, it always shows the whole
tree, and it appears once on the page. Four things many websites need cannot be built with it:

























What is missingWhat it is called hereA menu bar in the header whose entries open submenusvariant: dropdown or megaOnly the section you are reading in the sidebarscope: section”Previous” and “next” in reading order below the textvariant: pagerA sitemap in the footervariant: columns
And on a phone the menu bar should turn into something that fits in one hand — a menu behind a
burger button, for instance (mobile: offcanvas).
What this plugin does differently
One plugin, as many entries as you like. Every entry in quartz.config.yaml is a navigation of
its own with its own options. A website can carry a bar with the first level at the top, an
accordion with the current section on the left and a pager at the bottom — the same plugin three
times.
All of them read the same tree. It is built from the content folders at build time and computed
only once per build, however many navigations show it
(1.3).
The page has a say. Titles, order and visibility can be set in the configuration or in the
page’s own frontmatter — navOrder, navTitle, navHide, navIcon
(chapter 2).
What it does not do

It does not force you to replace the explorer. Both can sit side by side; they share no class
names and do not interfere. This website has replaced it all the same, with a list of its chapters
(8.1).
It knows no links that are not in the content folder. A menu item “GitHub” or “Imprint on
another domain” is not a page and appears in no tree. Quartz’s footer or a
layout box is the place for those.
It does not search. Search stays Quartz’s own.

en/1-getting-started/02-your-first-navig.title: 1.2 – Your first navigation
en/1-getting-started/02-your-first-navig.content:
Three steps, and the navigation is there.
1. Install the plugin
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
The command fetches the plugin and adds it to quartz.config.yaml — with every option and its
default value, as a tree in the left column (position: left, priority: 10). That is already
a working navigation. The long list may be shortened: whatever is not there, the plugin assumes as
its default.
In QuartzControl the same is done through the
marketplace.
2. Write the entry
A short entry for a menu bar in the header:
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: bar
      depth: 1
      mobile: offcanvas
    layout:
      position: header
      priority: 20

variant chooses the form — here a horizontal bar (chapter 4).
depth: 1 shows only the first folder level (3.2).
mobile: offcanvas turns it into a menu behind a burger button on phones
(chapter 6).
layout tells Quartz where the navigation goes. It is not part of the plugin but Quartz’s own
mechanism for every component. Without the block the navigation does not disappear: Quartz puts
it at the plugin’s default, left with priority: 10.

A second navigation is a second entry with the same source. More on that in
1.3.
3. Look
npx quartz build --serve
The bar sits in the header, the entry of the current page is highlighted, and every folder above it
carries the active-trail mark. Below the site’s mobile breakpoint
(6.2) the bar disappears behind a burger button.
When nothing appears





































What you seeWhat causes itNothing, on no page, no messageenabled: false.The navigation is on the left instead of where you wanted itThe layout block is missing or indented wrongly; the plugin’s default applies.Nothing on some pagesrootPath is set and the page lies outside it — that is hideOutsideRoot (3.2). Or scope finds no folder for this page (3.1).Nothing, but rootPath … is not a folder with visible pagesThe folder does not exist, or everything in it is hidden (9.2).A page is missing from the navigationDraft, unlisted, navHide or an exclude pattern (2.3).The order is wrong2.2 – Sorting.Folders and pages are called “index” or carry numbers2.1 – Titles and folder pages.

en/1-getting-started/03-what-happens-at-.title: 1.3 – What happens at build time
en/1-getting-started/03-what-happens-at-.content:
From entry to component
Quartz reads quartz.config.yaml and creates a component for every active entry — in the place
its layout block names, or without a block on the left with priority: 10. The plugin receives
the options exactly as they are written in the file and fills in everything missing from its own
defaults. A value it does not know — variant: vertikal, say — is replaced by the default and
reported once (9.2).
Two entries with identical options share one component in Quartz. That is harmless as long as
they sit in different places — except for element IDs, see
7.3.
From folder to tree
Quartz hands every component the list of all pages of the build. The tree is made from it:

Every page becomes a node. Its path (docs/setup) decides which folder it hangs in.
Every folder becomes a node whose link is the folder page — docs/index.
Hidden things drop out: tag pages, the 404 page, drafts, unlisted, navHide, exclude
(2.3).
Every node gets a title (2.1).
The children of every folder are sorted (2.2).
Empty folders drop out.

Folders can always be linked. Without an index.md, Quartz’s folder-page plugin creates the
folder page itself. It is in the same list and is treated like a real one — only its title comes
from the directory name.
One tree per build, not per navigation
The tree is computed once and then read by all navigations that share the tree-shaping options:
sorting, hiding, include/exclude, icons. Three entries that differ only in variant, scope or
depth cost one tree, not three. On a multilingual site it is one tree per language
(8.3).
One consequence is worth knowing: two navigations can place the same page differently if they
sort or hide differently. That is intended — a pager by date next to a sidebar in manual order is a
legitimate setup.
From tree and page to <nav>
For each page the navigation picks its part of the tree (chapter 3), marks
the current page with active and every folder above it with active-trail, and writes finished
HTML with relative links. Nothing is rebuilt in the browser. Switch JavaScript off and you get
the same navigation.
What the browser adds
One script — one for all navigations of the site — adds what HTML alone cannot do:





























WhatWhere it is neededRemember open folderspersistState (5.1)Open menus on hover, close them on Escape and on a click elsewheredropdown, mega, flyout (5.2)Redirect panels that would stick out of the window or a columnthe same threeHold the page still behind the mobile menu, Escapemobile: offcanvas (6.1)Navigate when an option is chosen in the jump menuselect, mobile: select
Stylesheet and script reach the site once, however many navigations are on it.

en/2-the-tree/01-titles-and-folder-pages.title: 2.1 – Titles and folder pages
en/2-the-tree/01-titles-and-folder-pages.content:
The title of a page
The plugin takes the first value it finds:

navTitle in the frontmatter
title in the frontmatter
the file name without .md — 01 First Steps, not the slug 01-first-steps
the last part of the slug

navTitle is for cases where the page title is too long for a navigation:
---
title: Installing on macOS, Linux and in containers
navTitle: Installation
---
The title of a folder
In the navigation a folder is a node whose link is its folder page (docs/index). Its title
comes from:

navTitle in its index.md
title in its index.md
the real directory name — 02 Guides, not 02-guides
the last part of the slug

If there is no index.md, Quartz’s folder-page plugin creates the folder page itself at build
time. The folder stays linkable; its title then comes from the directory name.


                  
                  Folder notes count as folder pages 
                  
                

A file named like its folder (docs/docs.md) and an _index.md already arrive in Quartz as
docs/index. For the plugin they are the same as an index.md.


A page and a folder with the same name
about.md next to a folder about/ gives two entries: the page about and the folder
about/index. To turn them into one, move the page into the folder as index.md.
Numbers in front of the name
Many vaults sort with numbers: 01 Getting started, 02 Guides. The number decides the order
(2.2) — in the title you usually do not want to see it.
options:
  stripNumericPrefix: true
This removes a leading number and the character after it — 01-, 01 , 01_, 01. — from the
title. The order stays, because it is read from the file or directory name, not from the title.


                  
                  It also hits titles from the frontmatter 
                  
                

The number is removed from every title that starts that way, not just from file names.
title: 1.2 – Your first navigation becomes 2 – Your first navigation: 1 is the number, .
the character after it. That is why this handbook does not switch the option on. The only
exception is navTitle — whatever is written there stays as it is.

en/2-the-tree/02-sorting.title: 2.2 – Sorting
en/2-the-tree/02-sorting.content:
What gets sorted is always the children of one folder among themselves. There are three methods:
options:
  sort: manual        # manual | alphabetical | date
  sortDirection: asc  # asc | desc
  foldersFirst: first # first | last | mixed
Folders first
Before any method comes foldersFirst: first puts folders before pages, last after them, mixed
sorts both together. Within the folders and within the pages the chosen method then applies.
manual — the cascade
The default. Four stages, each one only decides where the previous one was tied:






























StageSourceExample1the order list in the configurationorder: { docs: [intro, setup] }2navOrder in the frontmatternavOrder: 103the number in front of the file or directory name02 Setup.md4the titleSetup
Whoever has no value at a stage comes after everyone who has one. A page with navOrder therefore
comes before every page without — whatever number the other carries in its file name.
Without order, navOrder and numbers, the cascade gives an alphabetical order.
The order list
The order in one place instead of spread across many frontmatter blocks:
options:
  order:
    "": [docs, blog, about]      # the root
    docs: [intro, setup, faq]

The key is the folder path; "" is the root. docs, docs/, docs/index and docs.md mean the
same.
An entry is the last part of the slug (intro) or the file or directory name (01 Intro);
upper and lower case do not matter.
Whatever is not in the list follows after it, ordered by stages 2 to 4.
An entry that does not exist in the folder is reported once by the build
(9.2) — usually a typo or a renamed file.



                  
                   foldersFirst comes before the list
                  
                

With the default foldersFirst: first, folders come before pages even if the list says
otherwise. about in the example above is a page and therefore ends up after docs and blog,
wherever it is in the list. For the list alone to count, add foldersFirst: mixed.


navOrder
A number, smaller first. Decimals and negative values work, as does a number in quotes. In an
index.md, navOrder sets the position of the folder among its siblings. Tip: use steps of ten,
so something fits in between later.
Numbers
01 Intro, 02-setup, 3_faq, 4. Appendix — a number at the start, followed by -, _, . or a
space. The number is compared as a number, 10 comes after 9. Whether it stays visible in the
title is decided by stripNumericPrefix (2.1).
alphabetical
The title only. Compared naturally — Part 2 before Part 10 — and regardless of case or accents.
The language decides the order of letters. The plugin sorts with the locale from the
Quartz configuration: with de-DE, Ärger sits next to Apfel; with sv-SE, after Zebra. That
way every machine that builds the site sorts the same. On a multilingual site every tree sorts by its
language: with the site’s locale when it is the same language, otherwise with the language code
(8.3).
date
options:
  sort: date
  dateField: created    # created | modified | published
  sortDirection: desc   # newest first
The dates come from Quartz’s created-modified-date plugin; its configuration decides which date a
page has. Pages without a date come last; with equal dates the title decides.
The direction
sortDirection: desc reverses every stage, including the title. Missing values still stay at the
end: a blog with sort: date and desc lists undated posts after the dated ones, not before.
Two navigations, two orders
Every entry sorts on its own. A pager through the posts by date and a sidebar in manual order get
along — they then read two differently sorted trees
(1.3).

en/2-the-tree/03-hiding-and-selecting.title: 2.3 – Hiding and selecting
en/2-the-tree/03-hiding-and-selecting.content:
Hiding here means: not in the navigation. The page is still built and remains reachable through
its address, links and search. To not publish a page at all, use Quartz’s own means — draft,
ignorePatterns, explicit-publish.
What is missing by itself






























WhatOptionDefaultthe 404 page—always hiddenthe tags folder with the tag pageshideTagstruepages marked unlisted by the unlisted-pages pluginhideUnlistedtruedrafts, draft: truehideDraftstrue
hideDrafts only matters if drafts reach the build at all. With Quartz’s remove-draft plugin they
are gone before that.
navHide — the page decides
---
title: Imprint
navHide: true
---
In an index.md, navHide: true hides the whole folder, with everything in it. The field
understands true, false and the words yes/no.
include and exclude — the configuration decides
Patterns on slugs, that is on the path as it appears in the address — without .md, with hyphens
instead of spaces.
options:
  exclude:
    - private         # the folder private with everything in it
    - "drafts/**"     # everything below drafts
    - "*/archive"     # any page or folder archive one level deep





















CharacterMeaning*any number of characters within one path segment**any number of characters across path segments?exactly one character
A folder name hits the whole subtree. It is not just the slug itself that is tested but every
folder above it: docs matches docs/index, docs/setup and docs/guides/alpha.
include is the counterpart: if anything is listed there, only what matches stays. exclude is
checked first and wins.
options:
  include: [docs]   # a navigation for the documentation only


                  
                   docs/* takes the folder with it
                  
                

* matches every child of docs — including index, and through the folder check everything
below. Nothing is left, and the empty folder drops out. Hiding just the folder page
(exclude: ["docs/index"]), on the other hand, keeps the folder: it then links to its first page
(3.3).


Empty folders
Whatever is left after hiding gets tidied up:




















OptionDefaultEffecthideEmptyFolderstruefolders without visible children drop outkeepIndexOnlyFolderstrue… unless they have a folder page of their own
Because folder-page creates a page for every folder, a folder whose pages are all hidden stays with
the defaults — as a link to its folder page. If you do not want that, set
keepIndexOnlyFolders: false. The root never drops out.

en/2-the-tree/index.title: 2 – The tree
en/2-the-tree/index.content:
Every navigation shows part of the same tree. This chapter is about the tree itself — what is in it,
what it is called and in what order. Which part is shown is in chapter 3.





















PageContent2.1 – Titles and folder pagesWhere an entry gets its name, and what numbers do to it2.2 – SortingManual, alphabetical, by date — and the cascade behind it2.3 – Hiding and selectingWhat is left out by itself, navHide, include and exclude
The four frontmatter fields
A page can have a say in its own entry:






























FieldEffectIn an index.mdnavTitletitle in the navigation instead of titletitle of the foldernavOrdernumber for manual order, smaller firstposition of the folder among its siblingsnavHidetrue hides the pagehides the whole foldernavIconicon before the title (7.1)icon of the folder
The names can be changed with frontmatterKeys, for instance when a vault already uses order:
options:
  frontmatterKeys:
    order: order
    title: short

en/3-the-scope/01-rootpath-and-scope.title: 3.1 – rootPath and scope
en/3-the-scope/01-rootpath-and-scope.content:
Two options, two questions:

rootPath — from which folder does the navigation count at all? The default is the site root.
scope — which folder below it is shown, depending on the page you are on?

What is shown is always the children of the chosen folder, not the folder itself. To have it as a
header above, use showScopeRoot (3.2).
rootPath
options:
  rootPath: docs
The navigation starts at docs: its top level is guides, Intro and Setup. docs, docs/,
/docs/index and docs.md mean the same. If the folder does not exist — or everything in it is
hidden — the navigation stays empty, and the build says so once.
On pages outside rootPath, here blog/first-post, the navigation does not appear at all. That
is hideOutsideRoot (3.2).
scope

























scopeShown are the children of …root (default)rootPath — the same on every pagesectionthe first-level folder below rootPath that contains the pageparentthe folder that contains the pagecurrentthe folder that is the page — or, for an ordinary page, its folder
The difference between parent and current only shows on folder pages. Side by side, without
rootPath:















































Current pagerootsectionparentcurrentindex (start page)rootnothingrootrootdocs/indexrootdocsrootdocsdocs/02-setuprootdocsdocsdocsdocs/guides/indexrootdocsdocsdocs/guidesdocs/guides/alpharootdocsdocs/guidesdocs/guides
The table was checked against the plugin’s functions, not derived from the description.
When to use which

root for everything that looks the same on every page: menu bar, sitemap, explorer
replacement.
section for a sidebar that shows only the current section. The start page has no section, so
it stays empty there — the right column of this website shows exactly that.
parent for “this page’s neighbours”. On a folder page those are the neighbouring folders.
current for “what is in here”. On a folder page those are its children.

Together with rootPath
section counts the first level below rootPath. With rootPath: docs the section of
docs/guides/alpha is therefore docs/guides.
parent on the folder page of rootPath itself shows its children: the folder above would lie
outside, so the navigation takes rootPath.
Pages that are not in the tree
If the current page is hidden — tag page, navHide, an exclude pattern — or written in another
language than the tree, the tree does not know it.
Then:

















scopeResultrootThe navigation appears, just without a marked entry.section, parent, currentThe navigation does not appear — without a page there is no reference folder.
That is not a bug but a tool: this website gives its German chapter navigation language: de, the
English pages are not in it, and so no German navigation appears on English pages
(8.1).

en/3-the-scope/02-levels-and-headers.title: 3.2 – Levels and headers
en/3-the-scope/02-levels-and-headers.content:
depth — how deep
options:
  depth: 1   # 0 = unlimited (default)
Counted from the chosen folder (3.1): depth: 1 shows only
its children, depth: 2 their children too. Folders at the limit appear as a link without expanding.
The usual values:





























Wheredepthmenu bar bar1dropdown2 — first level in the bar, second in the menumega3 — bar, column headings, entriessitemap columns2sidebar tree, accordion0
depth also applies to select and pager: a pager with depth: 1 only pages through the first
level.
hideOutsideRoot — where it hides itself
Only effective with rootPath. With the default true, the navigation appears only on the folder
page of rootPath and on pages below it.
options:
  rootPath: docs
  hideOutsideRoot: false   # the docs navigation on the blog too
false is right for a footer sitemap that should show the same subtree everywhere. true is right
for anything that only makes sense in one section. One navigation per language needs no rootPath for
that (8.3).
showScopeRoot — a header
options:
  scope: section
  showScopeRoot: true
Above the list sits the shown folder itself, as a link. With scope: section that is the name of the
section — “1 – Getting started” above the pages of the first chapter, as on the right of this page.
Where the link points is decided by folderLink (3.3).
showHome — a “Home” entry
options:
  variant: bar
  depth: 1
  showHome: true
The first entry of the list leads to the folder page of rootPath, without rootPath to the start
page. It is labelled “Home” (or “Start”, depending on the language — 7.3), in the vertical variants
with a house in front. It only appears if that page exists, and never with tabs.
indexEntry — an “Overview” row
options:
  variant: accordion
  indexEntry: first
Every folder whose children are shown and which has a folder page gets the entry “Overview” as its
first child, leading to that page.
This is needed when the folder row itself is not a link: with the default folderClick: toggle
a click on the row only expands the folder (5.1). Without
indexEntry the folder page would then be unreachable from this navigation.

en/3-the-scope/03-where-folders-link.title: 3.3 – Where folders link
en/3-the-scope/03-where-folders-link.content:
options:
  folderLink: index   # index | first-child | none





















ValueA folder title leads to …index (default)its folder page; if there is none, its first pagefirst-childits first page, even if it has a folder pagenonenothing — the title is text
The first page
“First page” means: the first entry in tree order (2.2) that is a page.
If a subfolder is there, the plugin keeps looking inside it — unless it has a folder page of its own,
in which case that is the first page.
first-child suits folders that are only structure: a click on “Guides” lands directly on the first
guide instead of an overview that has nothing to say.
Are there folders without a page at all?
Rarely. Quartz’s folder-page plugin creates a page for every folder, even without index.md. The
fallback of index to the first page only applies when folder-page is switched off — or when the
folder page was hidden, for instance with exclude: ["docs/index"].
What the other variants make of it





















VariantFolder without link target (none)lists, bars, menustitle as textselectoption cannot be selectedpagerskipped
And one peculiarity of the pager: if a folder and its first page lead to the same address, it
pages there only once. A “Previous” that points at the page you are on does not exist.
Folders that expand
In accordion, flyout, dropdown and mega a folder is more than a title — it expands. Whether
its row then expands or links is decided by a second option, folderClick
(5.1). folderLink only says where a link leads, if there is
one.

en/3-the-scope/index.title: 3 – The scope
en/3-the-scope/index.content:
A bar in the header shows the first level of the whole site, a sidebar only the section you are
reading. Both read the same tree (chapter 2) — they just pick different
parts of it.





















PageContent3.1 – rootPath and scopeFrom which folder, and relative to the current page3.2 – Levels and headersdepth, hideOutsideRoot, showScopeRoot, showHome, indexEntry3.3 – Where folders linkFolder page, first page or no link at all
The examples in this chapter assume this site:
index.md
blog/
  first-post.md
docs/
  index.md
  01 Intro.md
  02 Setup.md
  guides/
    alpha.md
    beta.md

en/4-variants/01-vertical.title: 4.1 – Vertical
en/4-variants/01-vertical.content:
The three vertical variants carry a glyph on every row, like a file explorer: a folder, an open
folder, a page (7.1). Folder rows get smaller and lighter with each
level, so you can find where a branch begins.
tree
options:
  variant: tree
A nested list, everything visible. Nothing expands, nothing opens; a thin line guides the eye down
the levels. The current page gets a background colour and an accent bar.
Right when the scope is small — one chapter, one section. The right column of this website is a
tree with scope: section.
accordion
options:
  variant: accordion
  expandActive: true         # default: the path to the current page is open
  folderDefaultState: collapsed
  persistState: true         # remember open folders
The same list, but every folder can be expanded. It is built with <details> and <summary> — so it
works without JavaScript too. The path to the current page is open, everything else closed until you
open it.
Right for a whole site in the sidebar — the obvious replacement for the explorer. What a click on a
folder row does, and how to keep only one folder per level open, is in
5.1.
flyout
options:
  variant: flyout
  trigger: hover     # or click (default)
  flyout:
    side: auto       # auto | right | left
A list whose folders do not expand downwards but open a panel beside them — like an operating
system menu. Deeper folders open their panel beside again.
Which side: with side: auto the browser decides when opening. If the navigation sits in the right
half of the page, the panels open to the left, otherwise to the right. right and left fix it.
Right when a sidebar should stay narrow and the tree is deep.


                  
                  Panels in a column that scrolls 
                  
                

Sidebars often scroll on their own (overflow: auto) or fade out softly at the bottom. A panel
inside would be cut off. The script therefore lifts it out of the column when it opens and anchors
it to its row; when the column scrolls, it closes (5.2).


Which of the three?





















QuestionAnswerShould everything be visible at a glance?treeIs the tree large but the column tall?accordionIs the column narrow and the tree deep?flyout

en/4-variants/02-horizontal.title: 4.2 – Horizontal
en/4-variants/02-horizontal.content:
The four horizontal variants put the first level into a row. They differ in what happens to the
levels below. The row itself has no glyphs, and all entries are the same size.
bar
options:
  variant: bar
  depth: 1
A row of links. With depth: 1 that is the classic menu bar. If deeper levels are allowed, they sit
in the same row behind their folder, whose name then gets a colon. That works for two levels with
few entries, in a footer for instance; for more there is dropdown.
dropdown
options:
  variant: dropdown
  depth: 2
  trigger: click   # or hover
The first level in the row; a folder opens a menu below with its children. Deeper levels are
indented in the same menu. Pages on the first level are ordinary links.
A menu that would stick out of the window on the right is hung from the right edge of its entry by the
script. Opening one closes the other; Escape and a click elsewhere close all
(5.2).
mega
options:
  variant: mega
  depth: 3
  trigger: hover
  folderClick: link
Like dropdown, but the menu is wide and split into columns: the second level forms the column
headings, the third sits below them. Right for large sites with sections that each have several
subsections. The width is set by --quartz-nav-mega-min-width (7.2).
tabs
options:
  variant: tabs
  tabs:
    secondary: true   # default
The first level as tabs. If the current page lies in a first-level folder, its children appear in
a second row below. With secondary: false it stays at the tab row.
Right for sites with a few large sections between which you rarely switch. There is no showHome for
tabs — the tab row has no place for it.
align — aligning the row
options:
  align: center   # left (default) | center | right | full

























ValueResultleftentries at the startcenterentries in the middlerightentries at the endfullevery entry gets an equal share of the width
Applies only to bar, dropdown, mega and tabs; the other variants ignore the option. With
mobile: accordion or offcanvas the entries stack below the mobile breakpoint and the alignment
no longer applies; with the default mobile: same the row just wraps (chapter 6).
Which of the four?

























QuestionAnswerOnly the sections, no subpages?bar with depth: 1Sections with a handful of pages?dropdownSections with subsections?megaA few sections, and you should see which one you are in?tabs

en/4-variants/03-special-forms.title: 4.3 – Special forms
en/4-variants/03-special-forms.content:
columns
options:
  variant: columns
  depth: 2
layout:
  position: footer
The first level as column headings, their children below. The grid fills the width with as many
columns as fit at a minimum width of --quartz-nav-column-min-width (default 10rem). The classic
footer sitemap.


                  
                   columns.max
                  
                

The option is meant to limit the number of columns but currently has no effect — the grid
follows the width alone. For fewer columns, increase the minimum width.


select
options:
  variant: select
  title: Jump to
  select:
    button: false   # default
A <select> jump menu. First-level folders become option groups, their folder page appears in
them as “Overview”; deeper levels are indented. As long as the current page is not in the list, the
menu shows “Jump to…”.
How it navigates: chosen with the mouse, it goes right away. Chosen with the keyboard, it waits
for Enter — otherwise the page would jump while you arrow through the options. select.button: true
adds a “Go” button next to it, for sites that want an explicit step.
The menu navigates through Quartz’s own page transitions and needs JavaScript. Here title
becomes the menu’s label.
Often a select is not the navigation itself but its mobile version: mobile: select puts the same
menu in place of a list below the mobile breakpoint (6.1).
pager
options:
  variant: pager
layout:
  position: afterBody
“Previous” and “Next”, each with the title of the neighbouring page and an arrow. There is one below
every text on this website.
In what order
options:
  pager:
    order: tree   # tree (default) | siblings

















pager.orderPages through …treethe whole scope in reading order: folder page, then its children, then the next foldersiblingsonly the neighbours in the same folder; the end of the folder is the end
With tree the scope decides how far it goes (chapter 3):

scope: root pages through the whole site — or through rootPath.
scope: section stops at the end of the section.
depth limits the depth.

Folders without a link target are skipped, as is a folder that leads to the same page as its first
entry (3.3). On the first page “Previous” is missing, on the
last “Next”; if a page has neither, nothing appears.
Labels
options:
  pager:
    labels: false   # arrow and title only
The words “Previous” and “Next” follow the page’s language on a multilingual site, otherwise the
site’s language (7.3).

variant chooses the form. Every variant brings its own direction — vertical or horizontal —, there

en/5-interaction/01-folder-rows.title: 5.1 – Folder rows
en/5-interaction/01-folder-rows.content:
folderClick — expand or link
The whole row of an expandable folder is the click target. What it does is decided by
folderClick:
options:
  folderClick: toggle   # toggle (default) | link
toggle — a click anywhere on the row opens or closes the folder. The folder page can then only be
reached from this navigation through an extra entry: indexEntry: first puts “Overview” into the
folder as its first child (3.2).
link — the row is a link to the folder page, and a separate expand button with the chevron sits
at its right edge. That is the usual choice together with trigger: hover: the menu opens on hover,
the click follows the link (5.2).






























togglelinkClick on the titleexpandsopens the folder pageChevrona hint, not a button of its owna button of its own, always visibleFolder page reachable viaindexEntry: firstthe titleFor screen readersone control with the titlea link and a button “Expand …”


                  
                  Folders that only expand on mobile 
                  
                

With mobile: accordion, folders in tree, bar, tabs and columns expand only on phones
(6.1). They always use link and button, whatever folderClick
says — on the desktop their title should stay a link.


chevrons — the arrow
options:
  chevrons: false
Hides the chevron on folders with folderClick: toggle. With link it stays, because there it is the
button. Which symbol the chevron is, is set by iconNames.chevron (7.1).
Open or closed




















OptionDefaultEffectfolderDefaultStatecollapsedopen makes all folders start openexpandActivetruefolders on the path to the current page start open
Both apply to accordion. The menus of dropdown and mega and the panels of flyout always
start closed — a menu that is already open on load covers the page.
exclusive — one folder per level
options:
  variant: accordion
  exclusive: true
Opening a folder closes the open one next to it. The browser does this itself through the name
attribute of <details> — without a script, in current browsers. Older ones leave several open.
persistState — memory
options:
  variant: accordion
  persistState: true
  id: sidebar
Which folders someone opened or closed is remembered by the browser in localStorage and restored on
the next page. The path to the current page still stays open as long as expandActive applies —
a remembered “closed” does not win against the page you are on.


                  
                  With persistState, always an id
                  
                

It is stored under the navigation’s ID. Without id that is a checksum of all options — change any
of them later and the memory is gone. A fixed id keeps it across changes
(7.3).


Menus and panels (dropdown, mega, flyout) are never remembered.

en/5-interaction/02-click-or-hover.title: 5.2 – Click or hover
en/5-interaction/02-click-or-hover.content:
trigger
options:
  variant: dropdown
  trigger: hover   # click (default) | hover
  folderClick: link
Applies to dropdown, mega and flyout.
click opens a menu when its folder is clicked. That works everywhere, even without a script.
hover opens it on hover and — so keyboard users are not left out — also as soon as an entry
inside receives focus. On leaving it closes after a short delay, so a menu does not snap shut when the
mouse cuts a corner.
Hover only exists on devices that support it. On a phone or tablet click applies automatically.


                  
                   hover belongs with folderClick: link
                  
                

With toggle, a click closes the menu that hovering had already opened. With link, hovering opens
the menu and the click leads to the folder page — which is what you expect from a menu bar.


How menus close

Opening another one closes the open one on the same level.
A click elsewhere closes all menus of this navigation.
Escape closes all and puts focus back on the folder whose menu it came from.
A page change closes all before the new page appears.

Where a panel moves to
When a panel opens, the script checks whether it has room.
flyout in the right half. With flyout.side: auto the panels open to the left when the
navigation sits in the right half of the window — otherwise they would stick out. The chevron then
points left. right and left switch the check off.
dropdown and mega at the right edge. A menu that would stick out of the window on the right
hangs from the right edge of its entry instead of the left.
In a column that clips. If the sidebar scrolls on its own, or fades out softly at the bottom, it
would cut a panel off. The panel is then lifted out of the column — into the browser’s top layer, in
older browsers with a fixed position — and anchored to its row. Because a position anchored like that
does not move along when scrolling, it closes as soon as you scroll.

en/5-interaction/03-without-javascript.title: 5.3 – Without JavaScript
en/5-interaction/03-without-javascript.content:
The navigation is finished HTML when it arrives in the browser. The script adds things but changes
nothing the structure relies on.
What works without the script

en/6-mobile/01-the-five-modes.content:
options:
  variant: dropdown
  mobile: offcanvas   # same (default) | accordion | offcanvas | select | hidden





























mobileBelow the mobile breakpointsamestays as it is; a row wrapsaccordionbecomes a stacked list with expandable foldersoffcanvasdisappears behind a burger button and slides in as a panel from the leftselectbecomes a jump menuhiddendisappears
same
For everything that is narrow anyway: tree, accordion, pager, select. For a horizontal bar
only if it has very few entries.
accordion
A row becomes a list stacked vertically, and folders with children become expandable. On phones they
start closed — except the path to the current page and whatever persistState remembered. On the
desktop they stay open and their title a link; the expand button is invisible there.
Suits bar, tabs and columns, which otherwise have no expandable folders, and dropdown and
mega, whose menus move into the flow of the page on phones.
If someone rotates their tablet across the breakpoint, the folders follow — they close or open without
reloading the page.
offcanvas
options:
  variant: bar
  depth: 2
  mobile: offcanvas
layout:
  position: header
In place of the navigation there is a burger button. It opens a panel that slides in from the
left, with a close button at the top and a dimmed background behind it. The panel shows the navigation
as a stacked list with expandable folders, as with accordion.
The panel closes via the button, a click on the background, Escape or a page change. While it is
open, the page behind it does not scroll.
That is the usual choice for the menu bar in the header.


                  
                  Not in a column that holds its children 
                  
                

The panel sits fixed over the window (position: fixed). An ancestor with transform, filter or a
mask turns “over the window” into “over this ancestor” — the panel then appears squashed or cut off.
The header of a Quartz site is the safe place for it; a scrolling sidebar is not.


It can be operated by keyboard too: the switch behind the burger button is a checkbox that receives
focus and reports its state through aria-expanded.
select
The list gives way to a jump menu, as variant: select shows (4.3):
first-level folders as groups, folder pages as “Overview”. It does not get more compact — but you only
see the structure once you open the menu. Needs JavaScript.
Suits a large sidebar that would end up below the text on a phone.
hidden
The navigation disappears. Right when another navigation takes over its job on phones — a sidebar with
hidden next to a header bar with offcanvas, for instance. The chapter navigation of this website is
hidden; on phones the pager below the text remains.
Quartz’s own display
Quartz knows display: desktop-only and mobile-only in the layout block. It works similarly to
mobile: hidden but is applied by Quartz itself: the component is then wrapped in a container of its
own, and the breakpoint is Quartz’s. mobile: hidden hides the navigation itself and can honour a
different breakpoint from breakpoints (6.2).

en/6-mobile/02-breakpoints.title: 6.2 – Breakpoints
en/6-mobile/02-breakpoints.content:
Where the breakpoint comes from
Quartz 5 has no option for its breakpoints in quartz.config.yaml. They are in the project’s
quartz/styles/variables.scss:
$breakpoints: (
  mobile: 800px,
  desktop: 1200px,
);
The plugin reads this file when the build creates the navigation and puts the value into its
stylesheet and script. Move the site’s breakpoint, and you move it for all navigations too — without a
second place you could forget.
If the file cannot be read, the plugin uses Quartz’s defaults, 800 and 1200 pixels, and says so once
(9.2).
Mobile means: at most this wide. With mobile: 800px a window of exactly 800 pixels is already
mobile, one of 801 is not.


                  
                  Restart after a change 
                  
                

The file is read when the navigation is created, not for every page. After changing
variables.scss, restart npx quartz build --serve.


Overriding
options:
  breakpoints:
    mobile: 640px
Pixels, rem and em are allowed; a bare number counts as pixels. desktop is accepted but currently
used by no rule of the plugin.


                  
                  The same in every entry — or not at all 
                  
                

The plugin’s stylesheet applies to all navigations of a site, not to a single one. If only one
entry sets a different breakpoint, the stylesheet ends up on the site twice, once with each
breakpoint, and both apply to every navigation. Between the two values every navigation then looks
half mobile. If you need a different breakpoint, change it in variables.scss — or set
breakpoints to the same value in every entry.


How this fits the layout
Quartz’s own layout wraps at the same breakpoint, because it reads the same file. A navigation with
mobile: offcanvas therefore turns into a burger button exactly when the sidebars slide below the
text.
With layout frames from QuartzControl that is not the
case. A frame brings its own breakpoints, stored in the project’s .quartz-gui/layout-breakpoints.json,
and does not read variables.scss. This website is such a case: its frame goes mobile below 900
pixels, variables.scss says 800. All five entries therefore carry
options:
  breakpoints:
    mobile: 900px
— the same value in every entry, so the stylesheet lands on the site only once.

en/7-appearance/02-css-variables.title: 7.2 – CSS variables
en/7-appearance/02-css-variables.content:
Where to set them
In the project’s quartz/styles/custom.scss:
.quartz-nav {
  --quartz-nav-indent: 1.5rem;
  --quartz-nav-color-active: var(--tertiary);
}
That wins without higher specificity: Quartz puts every component’s CSS into a CSS layer
(@layer quartz-base), custom.scss not — and rules outside a layer beat rules inside one.
A single navigation
Every navigation carries its ID in the data-quartz-nav attribute:
.quartz-nav[data-quartz-nav="sidebar"] {
  --quartz-nav-bg-hover: transparent;
}
The ID is the value of id — without id, a checksum that changes with every option. So give a
navigation you style specifically an id (7.3).
Alternatively className adds classes of your own to the <nav>.
Colours and fonts

en/7-appearance/03-markup-and-accessibil.content:
The structure
nav.quartz-nav.quartz-nav--<variant>.quartz-nav--mobile-<mode>
  h3.quartz-nav__title                                  title
  div.quartz-nav__panel
    div.quartz-nav__root > a.quartz-nav__root-link       showScopeRoot
    ul.quartz-nav__list[data-level]
      li.quartz-nav__item.quartz-nav__item--page|--folder
        a.quartz-nav__link > icon + span.quartz-nav__text
        details.quartz-nav__folder > summary + ul        expandable folders

Depending on variant and mode there are also: button, background and close button of the mobile menu,
the jump menu, the two links of the pager. All classes carry the quartz-nav prefix; the explorer and
other components are not touched.
States

































Class / attributeWhereactive<li> and <a> of the current pagearia-current="page"link of the current pageactive-trailevery folder on the path to itquartz-nav__item--parentfolders whose children are shownquartz-nav__item--splitrows with a link and their own expand buttonquartz-nav--align-<value>horizontal variants
id
options:
  id: sidebar
Every navigation has an ID. Without id the plugin derives it from all options (nav- and a
checksum). You need a fixed id in three cases:

CSS for exactly this navigation — .quartz-nav[data-quartz-nav="sidebar"]. A checksum changes
with every option, and the selector would miss.
persistState — memory is stored under the ID. With a checksum it is gone after every option
change (5.1).
Two navigations with identical options on one page. They would have the same ID and therefore
the same element IDs — the burger button of one would open the menu of the other.

Letters, digits, - and _ are allowed; anything else becomes -.
Keyboard and screen reader

Every navigation is a <nav> with a name of its own: ariaLabel, otherwise title, otherwise
“Main navigation” — for the pager “Previous and next page”. With several navigations on one page,
each deserves its own ariaLabel or a title, so they can be told apart in the list of landmarks.
Expandable folders are <details> and <summary>. With folderClick: toggle the row is a
single control with the title; with link the title is a link and the button next to it is called
“Expand ”. No link sits inside a button.
Chevrons and icons are hidden from screen readers.
Menus close with Escape and return focus to their folder; trigger: hover also opens on keyboard
focus (5.2).
The mobile menu hangs on a focusable checkbox with aria-expanded and aria-controls; Escape
closes it and puts focus back.
The jump menu navigates by keyboard only on Enter, not while arrowing through.
Motion is dropped with prefers-reduced-motion.

The plugin’s words
“Main navigation”, “Overview”, “Home”, “Previous”, “Next”, “Jump to…”, “Go” and “Expand …” come with
the plugin in English and German. Which language it uses is decided on a multilingual site by the
language of the page (8.3), otherwise by the site’s locale:
German for de-DE and any other German variant such as de-AT, English for everything else.
title and ariaLabel can be changed; the others cannot. The plugin does not translate these two: on
a bilingual site a navigation with its own text therefore needs one entry per language. How this
website does that is in 8.1.

en/8-recipes/01-the-navigations-of-this-.title: 8.1 – The navigations of this site
en/8-recipes/01-the-navigations-of-this-.content:
Three navigations are visible on this page: the chapters in the left column, “In this
chapter” in the right one and the previous/next links below the text. On phones a menu
behind the burger button joins them. In the configuration they are five entries: chapter list, menu
and pager for both languages, the chapter tree per language.









































idVariantPlaceLanguagekapitel-listetreeleft column, desktop onlythe page’smenueaccordionburger menu, phones onlythe page’spagerpagerbelow the textthe page’skapitel-detreeright columnGermankapitel-entreeright columnEnglish
How the languages are laid out here
The German pages are in the root, the English ones under en/;
quartz-multilanguage recognises English by the
folder and gives every other page the default language, German. From that the navigation builds one
tree per language: the German one holds only the German pages, the English one only the English
pages, and without the folder en — en/1-getting-started appears in it as 1-getting-started. How
this works for every layout is in 8.3.
The pager
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: pager
      id: pager
      breakpoints:
        mobile: 900px
    layout:
      position: afterBody
      priority: 5
One entry for both languages. With the default language: auto the pager pages through the tree
of the language the page is written in: after the last German page nothing follows, not the English
start page.
The words come out right by themselves. “Previous” and “Next” on English pages, “Zurück” and
“Weiter” on German ones, and the name for screen readers likewise
(7.3). Neither labels: false nor an ariaLabel is
needed.
Despite priority: 5, the pager appears below the backlinks, as the last thing before the footer.
The backlinks belong to the custom-8 group, and this website’s layout frame puts that group into an
area of its own above the rest of afterBody. priority only orders within one area.
The chapter tree
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: tree
      language: en
      scope: section
      showScopeRoot: true
      title: In this chapter
      mobile: hidden
      id: kapitel-en
      breakpoints:
        mobile: 900px
    layout:
      position: right
      priority: 6
The German entry differs in language: de, in title and id.

Two entries, because title is text. The navigation translates the plugin’s words, but not a
heading of your own. Each language therefore gets its entry with a fixed language.
language: en always shows the English tree. On a German page the page is not in it,
scope: section finds no chapter, and the entry does not appear
(3.1). In the same way kapitel-de disappears on English
pages.
scope: section shows the chapter the page is in. The start page has none, so the top of the
column stays empty there. The chapter of an English page is 1-getting-started, not en, because
the English tree does not contain the language folder.
tree rather than accordion, because a chapter has three or four pages — nothing to expand.
showScopeRoot puts the chapter name above as a link.
title is the heading, and at the same time the name for screen readers.
mobile: hidden, because on phones the pager below the text is enough.
breakpoints: 900px in all five entries, because this website’s layout frame wraps at 900
pixels and not at the 800 from variables.scss (6.2).

All five entries share the same tree-shaping options. The build therefore computes two trees, one
per language, not five (1.3).
The chapter list instead of the explorer
  - source: "@quartz-community/explorer"
    enabled: false
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: tree
      depth: 1
      showHome: true
      mobile: hidden
      id: kapitel-liste
      className: nav-kapitel-liste
      breakpoints:
        mobile: 900px
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 30

One entry for both languages. Without a title there is no text of its own, and with
language: auto the list shows the nine German chapters on German pages and the nine English ones
on English pages.
depth: 1 shows only the chapters, not their pages. The work is shared: the left says where you
can go, the right where you are within the chapter. A whole tree on the left would show the pages of
the current chapter twice. The chapter you are reading is marked.
showHome puts “Home” in front, “Start” on German pages — each time the start page of the page’s
own language (3.2).
No folderClick: with depth: 1 there is nothing to expand; every row is a link to the chapter
page.
mobile: hidden, because the menu takes over on phones.

The menu on phones
On phones the right column is gone; “In this chapter” is hidden there. So that every page stays
reachable through the menu, it shows more than the chapter list — and is therefore an entry of its
own, because depth applies at every width:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: accordion
      showHome: true
      folderClick: link
      exclusive: true
      mobile: offcanvas
      id: menue
      className: nav-menue
      breakpoints:
        mobile: 900px
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 31

accordion with every page. The chapter of the current page is open, the page marked
(5.1).
exclusive keeps one chapter open at a time; nine open chapters would be 45 rows.
folderClick: link: the chapter name leads to the chapter page, the arrow next to it expands.
mobile: offcanvas puts the menu behind a burger button.

Phones only, and where the explorer was
The plugin has no “phones only” mode. The menu is therefore hidden on desktops by a file of its own,
through the class from className. The same file puts the burger in the right place: this website’s
template is cut to the explorer; below 900 pixels the header keeps a gap on the left for its button,
and the left column has no height there. Left alone, the burger would sit on top of the breadcrumbs.
The file is quartz/styles/custom/plugin-navigations.scss, included in custom.scss next to the
template’s other files:
@media not all and (max-width: 900px) {
  .quartz-nav.nav-menue {
    display: none;
  }
}
 
@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .quartz-nav.quartz-nav--mobile-offcanvas {
    --quartz-nav-offcanvas-width: var(--tpl-drawer-width);
 
    .quartz-nav__burger {
      position: fixed;
      top: calc((var(--tpl-header-h) - var(--tpl-target)) / 2);
      inset-inline-start: var(--tpl-space-xs);
      z-index: 101;
    }
 
    .quartz-nav__close {
      display: none;
    }
  }
}

not all and (max-width: 900px) is the exact negation of the plugin’s query. min-width: 901px
would leave a window 900.5 pixels wide without either entry (6.2).
The --tpl-* variables belong to the template. The burger thereby sits where the explorer’s
button used to sit and stays visible above the open menu; a second tap closes it, which is why the ✕
goes (6.1).
Also in the file: the drawer’s background, rounding and shadow, so it looks like the explorer’s.

What is not switched on here
stripNumericPrefix. The titles of this website start with their number — “8.1 – The navigations …” —
and the option would take “8.” off (2.1). Sorting is
still right: by the numbers of the file and folder names, 01-…, 02-….

en/8-recipes/02-a-docs-site.title: 8.2 – A docs site
en/8-recipes/02-a-docs-site.content:
Documentation with a few sections, each with some chapters:
index.md
getting-started/ index.md, installation.md, first-steps.md
guides/          index.md, import/…, export/…
reference/       index.md, cli.md, configuration.md

The four entries
plugins:
  # 1 · Header: the sections, their pages in the menu, behind the burger button on phones
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: dropdown
      depth: 2
      trigger: hover
      folderClick: link
      mobile: offcanvas
      ariaLabel: Sections
      id: header
    layout:
      position: header
      priority: 20
 
  # 2 · Sidebar: only the section you are reading
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: accordion
      scope: section
      showScopeRoot: true
      persistState: true
      mobile: hidden
      ariaLabel: This section
      id: section
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 20
 
  # 3 · Below the text: paging, but not beyond the section
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: pager
      scope: section
      id: pager
    layout:
      position: afterBody
      priority: 10
 
  # 4 · Footer: the whole site in columns
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: columns
      depth: 2
      mobile: accordion
      ariaLabel: Sitemap
      id: sitemap
    layout:
      position: footer
      priority: 10
Why like this
Every navigation has one job. The header says which sections exist. The column says where you are
within a section. The pager says what comes next. The footer is where you look when you are lost.
Header: depth: 2 keeps the menu flat — sections and what they contain. Subfolders such as
import appear as a row linking to their folder page, their pages do not. hover with link
opens on hover and leads to the section page on click (5.2). On
phones the whole bar becomes a burger menu.
Column: scope: section shows only guides while you read the guides. The start page has no
section; the column stays empty there, and that is right — the header shows all sections.
mobile: hidden, because the burger menu does the same job on phones.
Pager: with scope: section, paging ends at the last chapter of the section instead of silently
jumping into the next one.
Footer: mobile: accordion collapses the columns into a list on phones whose sections can be
opened.
ariaLabel everywhere except on the pager, because three of the four <nav> would otherwise be
called “Main navigation”; the pager is called “Previous and next page” on its own
(7.3).
And the explorer?
Switch it off — enabled: false on the @quartz-community/explorer entry. The column takes over its
job for the current section, the header for the rest.
Variations

























If …then …the sections have many subfoldersheader as mega with depth: 3there are only three or four sections and you should see which one you are inheader as tabs, no menu thenthe order of the sections should not be alphabeticalorder: { "": [getting-started, guides, reference] } in all entries, or navOrder in the index.md filesthe pager should lead through the whole documentationleave out scope on the pager

en/8-recipes/03-more-recipes.title: 8.3 – More recipes
en/8-recipes/03-more-recipes.content:
Replacing the explorer
  - source: "@quartz-community/explorer"
    enabled: false
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: accordion
      folderClick: link
      persistState: true
      stripNumericPrefix: true
      mobile: offcanvas
      id: explorer
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 30
Like the explorer, but with folder rows that lead to their page, an order of your own
(2.2) and a burger menu on phones. The fixed id keeps the memory across
later option changes.
stripNumericPrefix only if the titles do not start with a number themselves
(2.1).
A blog by date
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: pager
      rootPath: blog
      sort: date
      sortDirection: desc
      ariaLabel: Newer and older post
      id: blog-pager
    layout:
      position: afterBody
      priority: 10
Visible only below blog, newest first. Note: with desc, “Previous” is the newer post and “Next”
the older — the order of the list, not of time. Posts without a date come last. A sidebar in manual
order gets along with it (1.3).
Multilingual sites
With quartz-multilanguage, one entry shows the
tree of each page’s language on every page, with no further option:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: accordion
      id: navigation
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 30
That holds for all four layouts quartz-multilanguage knows:

























LayoutExampleLanguage foldersde/docs/setup.md, en/docs/setup.mdDefault language in the rootdocs/setup.md, en/docs/setup.mdLanguage suffix in the file namedocs/Setup.md, docs/Setup.en.mdLanguage in the frontmatterblog/hallo.md with lang: de, blog/hello.md with lang: en
quartz-multilanguage stores on every page its language and a path without language folder or suffix:
en/docs/setup and docs/setup.en both become docs/setup. The navigation places pages by that path
but links to the real ones. Generated folder pages, which carry no language, get into the right
language through the pages next to them.

Paths in the options are language-neutral. rootPath: docs, order, nodeIcons and
include/exclude apply to every language alike. include and exclude also match the real path,
so exclude: [en] leaves out the English pages.
The plugin’s words and alphabetical sorting follow the page
(7.3, 2.2).
Your own texts do not. title and ariaLabel read the same in every language. If you need a
heading, add one entry per language with a fixed language — like the chapter tree of this website
(8.1).
A language folder’s start page (de/index.md) wins over an index.md in the root.

The option language





















ValueEffectauto (default)the tree in the language of the current pagea language code such as de or en-USalways that language’s tree; en-US finds pages marked enallno languages: one tree with every page, language folders as folders — the behaviour up to version 0.2
A code no page carries yields no navigation and a message (9.2). Pages
that belong to several languages or to none — a folder page shared by suffix pages, tag pages — get
the default language, the way quartz-multilanguage decides for them (9.3).
Entries per language folder from version 0.2
Up to version 0.2 every language needed its own entry, with rootPath: en or exclude: [en]. Such
entries keep working: a rootPath that names a language folder shows that language’s tree from the
folder on, and with hideOutsideRoot only on pages inside it. include: [en] has the same effect. The
separate entries are only needed for your own texts now.
Sections as tabs above the text
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: tabs
      align: full
      mobile: select
      ariaLabel: Sections
      id: tabs
    layout:
      position: beforeBody
      priority: 5
The sections as tabs across the full width, the pages of the active section in the second row. On
phones a jump menu instead of two rows that wrap.
A jump menu on phones only
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: tree
      depth: 2
      mobile: select
      title: Contents
      id: contents
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 30
On the desktop a tree in the column, on phones a single select field that takes hardly any room. The
title sits above in both versions.
A sitemap for part of the site only
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: columns
      rootPath: docs
      hideOutsideRoot: false
      depth: 2
      title: Documentation
      id: docs-sitemap
    layout:
      position: footer
      priority: 10
hideOutsideRoot: false shows the documentation in the footer on every page of the site, not only
inside docs (3.2).

en/9-reference/02-messages.title: 9.2 – Messages
en/9-reference/02-messages.content:
All messages start with [navigations] and appear once per cause, not once per page. None of them
stops the build: the plugin takes the default or leaves out what is broken and keeps building.
Unknown value "…" for `…`; using `…`.
A value the option does not know — a typo, a German spelling (variant: baum), a value from another
option. The named default applies. The allowed values are in 9.1.
`…` must be an integer >= …; using ….
depth or columns.max is not an integer, or too small. depth: "2" in quotes works; depth: 1.5 and
depth: -1 do not.
Ignoring invalid `…` entry …
An entry in include, exclude or an order list is not text or is empty. Only that entry is dropped.
`order` must be a map of folder → list. · `nodeIcons` must be a map of path → icon.
The option is a list instead of a map. Correct:
order:
  docs: [intro, setup]
nodeIcons:
  docs: lucide:book-open
Ignoring invalid `nodeIcons` entry for "…".
The value for this path is empty or not text.
`order` for "…" lists unknown entry "…".
A folder’s order list names something that does not exist in it — usually a renamed file, or a slug
instead of a file name with different spelling. The other entries still apply. See
2.2.
`rootPath: …` is not a folder with visible pages.
The folder does not exist, rootPath names a page instead of a folder, or everything in it is hidden —
by exclude, navHide, drafts. The navigation appears on no page.
`language: …` matches no page language (…).
The fixed language matches none of the languages quartz-multilanguage recorded on the pages; the
parentheses list the ones that exist. Usually a typo, or a language that has no page yet. The navigation
appears on no page (8.3).
Unknown Lucide icon `…`; see lucide.dev/icons
A name from navIcon, nodeIcons or iconNames is not in the Lucide set. No icon appears there.
Common causes: a name from an older Lucide version (home is house today), or with iconNames a
superfluous lucide: in front.
Could not read quartz/styles/variables.scss; using 800px / 1200px as breakpoints.
The build is not running in the project folder, or the file is missing. The navigation switches to
mobile at 800 pixels (6.2).
`variant: vertical` is now `tree`. · `dropdownTrigger` is now `trigger`.
Old spellings from version 0.1. They still work; the message goes away as soon as the new spelling is
used.
`style` was removed; …
The style option no longer exists and is skipped. Styling is done through the CSS variables
(7.2).
When nothing happens at all
No message, no navigation — then it is rarely the plugin:

























CauseWhat helpsenabled: falseswitch itThe scope is empty on this pagecheck scope, rootPath, hideOutsideRoot (3.1)The pager has no neighboursthe page is hidden, or it is the only one in the scopeThe navigation sits in an unexpected placelayout block missing — then left, priority: 10

en/9-reference/03-limits.title: 9.3 – Limits
en/9-reference/03-limits.content:
Only pages from the content folder
A menu item that leads to another website is not a page and appears in no tree. Quartz’s footer
(links) or a layout box is there for that.
The words exist only in German and English
“Previous”, “Next”, “Overview”, “Home” and the names for screen readers come with the plugin in these
two languages; every other language gets English. Only title and ariaLabel can be changed, and the
plugin does not translate them (7.3).
Shared pages get the default language
Tag pages and folder pages shared by several languages belong to no language. There the navigation
shows the tree of quartz-multilanguage’s default language — even on the tag page of an English tag. If
every page lives in a language folder, the site’s locale decides instead
(8.3).
With the language in the frontmatter, only one language has a start page
The index.md in the root belongs to exactly one language. The other language’s tree has no start
page: showHome and showScopeRoot with scope: root show nothing there.
detection with frontmatter before folder
If you reorder detection in quartz-multilanguage that way, pages in a language folder that carry lang
in the frontmatter keep the folder in their path; the others lose it. The English tree then shows
docs twice: in the root and under en. With the default [folder, suffix, frontmatter] this does
not happen.
breakpoints does not apply to a single navigation
The stylesheet is one for all. Different values in different entries end up as two stylesheets on the
site, both acting on every navigation (6.2).
stripNumericPrefix also hits titles from the frontmatter
Not only titles from file names but every title that starts with a number and -, _, . or a
space. “1.2 – Getting started” becomes “2 – Getting started”. Only navTitle stays untouched
(2.1).
columns.max has no effect
The option is accepted, but the grid follows the width only (4.3).
The jump menu needs JavaScript
select and mobile: select navigate through a script. Without JavaScript an option can be chosen,
but nothing happens (5.3).
No custom icons in the jump menu
An option of a <select> can only hold text (7.1).
One order per navigation, not per page
Sorting applies to an entry’s whole tree. A page cannot ask to sit somewhere else in one navigation than
in another — unless the two navigations sort differently.
Hover only with a mouse
trigger: hover works on devices that report hover. On touch devices the click opens.
The mobile menu needs a clear path
It sits over the window with position: fixed. Inside an ancestor with transform, filter or a mask
it gets squashed or cut off (6.1).
exclusive depends on the browser
One folder per level through the name attribute of <details> is supported by current browsers. Older
ones leave several folders open — the navigation still works.
Memory depends on the ID
persistState stores under the id. Without a fixed id, every option change changes the ID and what
was remembered is gone (5.1). It is stored in the visitor’s
browser; another browser, a private window or cleared site data start from scratch.
Folders are remembered under their real path. With language folders, de/docs and en/docs are two
folders, and memory starts afresh after switching language; with language suffixes both languages share
one folder and with it what was open.

en/index.title: Navigations
en/index.content:
Quartz ships one navigation: the explorer, a folder tree in the sidebar. That’s it.
quartz-navigations builds every other navigation a website needs from the same folder
structure — a menu bar in the header, an accordion for the current section, a sitemap in the
footer, “previous” and “next” below the text. One plugin, as many entries as you like, and each
one chooses which part of the tree it shows and in what form.
The navigation is built entirely at build time and works without JavaScript. A small script
adds what cannot be done without it: remembered folders, menus that open on hover, the scroll lock
behind a mobile menu.


                  
                  This website is its own proof 
                  
                

It is built with the plugin. The chapters in the left column, the menu on phones, “In this chapter”
in the right column and the previous/next links below every text are five entries of the plugin.
8.1 shows them and explains every option.


The nine chapters













































ChapterThe question it answers1 – Getting startedWhy the plugin, and how does the first navigation come about?2 – The treeWhere do titles and order come from, and what is left out on purpose?3 – The scopeThe whole site, one section or just the current folder?4 – The ten variantsTree, bar, accordion, menu, columns, pager — which one for what?5 – InteractionWhat happens when a folder is clicked, and what on hover?6 – MobileWhat becomes of a menu bar on a phone?7 – AppearanceIcons, colours, spacing — and how to change them8 – RecipesFinished combinations, one of them on this page9 – ReferenceEvery option, every message, every limit
In one minute
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
Then one entry per navigation. This one puts the first folder level into the header as a bar:
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: bar
      depth: 1
      mobile: offcanvas
    layout:
      position: header
      priority: 20
The details are in 1.2 – Your first navigation.
Where else it is written down
The short version is the repository README. The
sister plugins quartz-layout-box and
quartz-multilanguage work together with this one;
all three belong to QuartzControl, but the app is not
required.

index.title: Navigations
index.content:
Quartz bringt eine Navigation mit: den Explorer, einen Ordnerbaum in der Seitenspalte. Mehr nicht.
quartz-navigations baut aus derselben Ordnerstruktur jede weitere Navigation, die eine Website
braucht — eine Menüleiste im Kopf, ein Akkordeon für den aktuellen Bereich, eine Sitemap in der
Fußzeile, „Zurück“ und „Weiter“ unter dem Text. Ein Plugin, beliebig viele Einträge, und jeder
wählt selbst, welchen Ausschnitt des Baums er in welcher Form zeigt.
Die Navigation entsteht vollständig beim Bauen und funktioniert ohne JavaScript. Ein kleines
Skript ergänzt, was ohne es nicht geht: gemerkte Ordner, Menüs beim Überfahren, die Scroll-Sperre
hinter einem mobilen Menü.


                  
                  Diese Website ist ihr eigener Beleg 
                  
                

Sie ist mit dem Plugin gebaut. Die Kapitel in der linken Spalte, das Menü auf dem Telefon, „In diesem
Kapitel“ in der rechten Spalte und „Zurück / Weiter“ unter jedem Text sind fünf Einträge des Plugins.
8.1 zeigt sie und begründet jede Option.


Die neun Kapitel













































KapitelDie Frage, die es beantwortet1 – EinstiegWozu das Plugin, und wie steht die erste Navigation?2 – Der BaumWoher kommen Titel und Reihenfolge, und was fehlt absichtlich?3 – Der AusschnittDie ganze Site, ein Bereich oder nur der aktuelle Ordner?4 – Die zehn DarstellungenBaum, Leiste, Akkordeon, Menü, Spalten, Pager — welche wofür?5 – BedienungWas passiert beim Klick auf einen Ordner, und was beim Überfahren?6 – MobilWas wird aus einer Menüleiste auf dem Telefon?7 – AussehenIcons, Farben, Abstände — und wie man sie ändert8 – RezepteFertige Kombinationen, eine davon auf dieser Seite9 – NachschlagenAlle Optionen, alle Meldungen, alle Grenzen
In einer Minute
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
Dann je Navigation ein Eintrag. Dieser setzt die erste Ordnerebene als Leiste in den Kopf:
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: bar
      depth: 1
      mobile: offcanvas
    layout:
      position: header
      priority: 20
Ausführlich steht das unter 1.2 – Die erste Navigation.
Wo es sonst noch steht
Die Kurzfassung ist die README des Repositorys.
Die Schwesterplugins quartz-layout-box und
quartz-multilanguage arbeiten mit diesem zusammen;
alle drei gehören zu QuartzControl, nötig ist die App
aber nicht.
